summary.headline: M1-v2 (m1v2-s1 g20 best_so_far, A17.2 headline learned arm) vs ramjet (val-best baseline): segment mean clipped log-ratio +0.0316 (SE 0.0093), 10/12 segments ahead, one-sided exact Wilcoxon p = 0.0017 (< 0.05: PASS), P(learned > baseline) 0.833 with segment-bootstrap CI [0.583, 1.000] (significant and meaningful), geometric-mean segment ratio 1.0321; the segment mean is below the pre-registered MDE 0.0382
summary.caveats: in AIS-timed simulation only; sessions segments are at ceiling (deltas ~0); the token-weighted A19 metric is mixed (segment mean -0.0092 driven by fast25_synthetic:x0 -0.29, 10/12 segments ahead, p 0.032); significance is lost at tighter SLO scales 0.5 and 0.75 (sign kept); every learned arm carries LR-13 concentration/segregation/long-request flags (M1-v2: share above cap on 24/60 cells, NMI > 0.10 on 19, >=32K sacrifice on 11, dump workers on 5)

secondary_metrics.status: SECONDARY, descriptive, not pre-registered: computed after the single test pass from its cached records and per_request rows, no replay; never selects a policy or decides the headline

definitions.rec.*: harness record fields (learned_routing.goodput): percentiles over every completed request of the replay, warm-up and drain included; itl_p50/p90 are percentiles of per-request mean ITL; itl_tok_p99 is the native per-token ITL p99; throughput_tok_s = output tokens/s over the makespan; prefix_reuse = native prefix_cache_reused_ratio; rec.isl[b].* = the record's isl_buckets (good_frac_window is windowed)
definitions.win.*: the same latencies over exactly the requests the record's goodput window scores (learned_routing.window_guards.in_window_flags; in-window good count asserted equal to window_good on all 6,120 records), completed only
definitions.traj.*: AgentX only: per-play trajectory latency = last terminal_time_ms - first arrival_time_ms over the play's rows (tool gaps included); all = every play of the replay (identical play set for every policy, checked); win = plays starting at or after window_start_ms and finishing before window_end_ms
definitions.paired: per (cell, k) ln(A/B) (log) or A - B (diff), mean over k per cell, mean over a segment's cells, then over the 12 segments; positive = A higher
definitions.compact: [segment_mean, segments_higher, segments] (facts/test_results.json all-policy matrices, CORE metrics only; everything else is in facts/secondary_metrics_test.json)
definitions.|n>=20: small-sample sensitivity (chosen after seeing the per-bucket counts, descriptive): a bucket percentile is paired only if the bucket holds >= 20 requests in BOTH arms' record (win: completed in-window requests)

items.text: TTFT (A2.2: reported, not part of 'good'), M1-v2 vs ramjet on test, harness record fields over every completed request: p50 log-ratio +0.006 (x1.006), higher on 9 of 12 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.4697 (descriptive); p90 log-ratio -0.002 (x0.998), higher on 6 of 12 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.7910 (descriptive); p99 log-ratio -0.082 (x0.921), higher on 4 of 12 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.2661 (descriptive); so overall TTFT is on par. Long prompts are slower under M1-v2: TTFT p90 for 32K-64K prompts log-ratio +0.135 (x1.145), higher on 11 of 12 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.0122 (descriptive); counting only records with >= 20 such prompts in both arms log-ratio +0.169 (x1.184), higher on 8 of 8 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.0078 (descriptive); over the scored in-window requests with the same filter log-ratio +0.143 (x1.154), higher on 8 of 8 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.0078 (descriptive). By family (in-window, filtered, mean over cells of the log-ratio): agentx +0.013, fast25_conversation +0.970, fast25_synthetic +0.160, mooncake +0.367. Synthetic-sessions records hold at most 13 prompts of 32K-64K, so their bucket percentiles are not informative (in-window without the filter: log-ratio +0.026 (x1.026), higher on 9 of 10 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.0840 (descriptive)). >=64K prompts, filtered: log-ratio +0.021 (x1.021), higher on 3 of 7 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 1.0000 (descriptive) (by family agentx -0.114, fast25_conversation +0.734, fast25_synthetic +0.011, mooncake +0.237). Against default@defaults TTFT is much lower overall: p50 log-ratio -0.573 (x0.564), higher on 0 of 12 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.0005 (descriptive), p90 log-ratio -0.452 (x0.636), higher on 1 of 12 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.0024 (descriptive); but its 32K-64K p90 (filtered) is only log-ratio -0.011 (x0.989), higher on 3 of 8 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 1.0000 (descriptive), while ramjet's is log-ratio -0.180 (x0.835), higher on 2 of 8 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.0547 (descriptive). Ranked by that log-ratio vs default (lowest first) over the 32 non-default policies: ramjet 2, M1-v2 25; the other router-observable learned arms: m1 -0.075 (rank 17), m1noaff -0.057 (rank 20), m2r2 -0.040 (rank 22), ablam1 -0.075 (rank 16), m1cont -0.033 (rank 23).

Good fraction in window by ISL bucket, M1-v2 minus ramjet: 0-2048 +4.3 pp, higher on 8 of 12 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.1294 (descriptive); 2048-8192 +4.3 pp, higher on 8 of 12 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.0640 (descriptive); 8192-32768 -1.7 pp, higher on 7 of 12 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.2661 (descriptive); 32768-65536 -3.8 pp, higher on 5 of 10 segments; 65536- -3.7 pp, higher on 4 of 8 segments. M1-v2's request-count gain comes from short and mid prompts while long prompts lose goodput against ramjet (the LR-13 / A19 trade, now with its TTFT dimension).

Other PLAN secondary metrics, M1-v2 vs ramjet: end-to-end latency p90 of the scored in-window requests log-ratio -0.048 (x0.953), higher on 3 of 12 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.0093 (descriptive); per-request mean ITL p90 log-ratio +0.006 (x1.006), higher on 3 of 12 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.1294 (descriptive); native per-token ITL p99 log-ratio -0.077 (x0.926), higher on 4 of 12 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.0522 (descriptive); output throughput log-ratio +0.006 (x1.006), higher on 7 of 12 segments (open-loop cells are bound by the offered load); prefix reuse log-ratio -0.024 (x0.976), higher on 1 of 12 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.0010 (descriptive); AgentX per-play trajectory latency, all plays: mean log-ratio -0.012 (x0.988), higher on 0 of 4 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.1250 (descriptive), p90 log-ratio -0.004 (x0.996), higher on 1 of 4 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.2500 (descriptive); plays inside the window: mean log-ratio -0.016 (x0.984), higher on 0 of 4 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.1250 (descriptive). Vs default@defaults: prefix reuse log-ratio +0.238 (x1.268), higher on 12 of 12 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.0005 (descriptive), AgentX trajectory mean log-ratio -0.042 (x0.959), higher on 0 of 4 segments, two-sided exact Wilcoxon p 0.1250 (descriptive). All descriptive, not pre-registered; every finalist's row is in secondary_metrics.

Word the headline as 'M1-v2 beats the branch's ported heuristics, each tuned with an equal budget' (pre-registered test, p 0.0017), not 'beats every heuristic' and not 'learning beats the best available heuristic'. The baseline pool omits faithful LMetric (CONTRACT A2.5 excluded paper-faithful variants; LR-04: the `lmetric` port lacks the queued-prefill term), while M1-v2's class contains it and its s3 restart started at default + 20.7 x faithful LMetric.

Carry the val-only table of facts/fairness_in_class_heuristic.json, labeled 'auditor diagnostic, not pre-registered, never used for selection, test not evaluated': fresh val k3-10 objective M1-v2 0.1783, default + 10 x faithful LMetric (train-tuned, 8 evaluations) 0.1609, M1-v2 s3 start (untuned) 0.1612, faithful LMetric alone (untuned) 0.1490, ramjet 0.1411. Untuned faithful LMetric beats all 11 tuned baselines on val k0-2 (0.1493 vs at most 0.1423, ablabase) and on val k3-10. Default + faithful LMetric reproduces 53-66% of M1-v2's fresh-val margin over ramjet (M1-v2 vs ramjet cell +0.0372, segment +0.0290).

The learned increment over default + faithful LMetric is about +0.011 per segment on fresh val k3-10 (SE 0.0065, 5/6 segments; cell +0.0174, SE 0.0069), about 0.29 x the MDE 0.0382; it has NOT been measured on test (single-pass). A pre-registered follow-up adding faithful LMetric and SMetric baselines (equal budget, fresh segments or the A13 live runs, never the frozen test cells) is escalated to the operator.
